topics.topic: State 3 ownership and capability orchestration for reading owner requests, importing file streams, rendering failures, and closing connections
questions: Which State 3 module owns `serve_owner_request`, who calls it, and which capability performs the ordered steps of handing the file stream to `migration_import`, rendering `file_unreadable`, and closing the connection after the response?
Which named module capability reads each body or upload head and detects this failure before handing a request to operations?
Who hands the file stream to migration_import, and through which capability, while preserving operations’ stage-(1) owner-session and CSRF checks?
Which module owns closing the per-request connection, what capability performs it, and who calls that capability after an early body failure or after rendering file_unreadable?

quotes:
`module:owner_interface`. The owner interface: server-rendered, script-free
forms over the owner's operations (R0-29, A19).

One HTTP request from the owner's browser: the session cookie, the form's
fields with their CSRF value, a confirmation value where the step carries
one, the revision or access version the rendered card carried; for an
upload, a multipart body whose first part is the CSRF field and whose second
is the file (owner, 2026-11-17). `upload_framing.read_upload_head` reads
the body's head alone and answers the CSRF value and the file part's
declared length; `owner_interface` hands that length and the file part, as
an unread stream that ends where the part ends, to
`operations.perform_owner_operation`, without reading or buffering it.

After an upload's answer, whatever it was — accepted, or refused before any
or after some bytes were read — `owner_interface` discards the unread
remainder of the body without reading it into anything and closes the
connection its listener accepted; a connection that carried an upload is
never reused.

`module:upload_framing`. Read an upload's multipart head alone, so that its
CSRF value travels in the form and the file reaches `migration_import`
unread (A13 rules 5, 7; owner, 2026-11-17).

The file part's stream is a `MultipartFileBody`, the class
`upload_framing` owns that implements `UploadBody` (State 6); it fails
when the request's stream ends before the closing delimiter, which
`migration_import.read_import_mapping` refuses as `file_unreadable`, as any
stream that fails.
judgement.why: State 5 names `serve_owner_request`'s owner and caller and assigns upload-head reading, the handoff through operations, refusal rendering, unread-body disposal, and connection closure.

topics.topic: Whether an unreadable ordinary owner form with a valid session resets the idle timeout
questions: When an ordinary owner form carries a valid session but its body fails before the surface can hand a request to `operations`, does its arrival restart the session's 30-minute idle period?
Does an ordinary owner-interface request carrying a valid session restart the idle period when its form body cannot be read and therefore never reaches `operations`?

basis:
The owner opens the owner interface and signs in with the owner credential;
then makes requests in the session, signs out, or leaves it to expire.

`module:owner_interface` renders the sign-in form and every page, sets and
reads the session cookie and carries the CSRF value in every form; it decides
nothing (A13 rules 1, 5, 7). `module:operations` hands each request to
`module:owner_sessions`, which owns all of A13: the credential check, the
count and the lockout, the session, its limits, its locks, its CSRF value and
its pending confirmation.

A surface whose reading of a body
fails before it has a request to hand on — a form, a service request, an
upload's head — answers nothing: the connection is closed and nothing reaches

topics.topic: Whether a confirmation value is consumed when a later body read fails
questions: If a form exposes a valid CSRF value and the pending confirmation value before a later part of its body fails, is that confirmation value consumed?

quotes:
A surface whose reading of a body
fails before it has a request to hand on — a form, a service request, an
upload's head — answers nothing: the connection is closed and nothing reaches
`operations`.

A submission
   carries it when it passes the owner session and CSRF checks (A04 rule 6,
   stage 1) and gives a value equal to the pending one; from there on,
   whatever the answer — a binding to another action or input included — the
   pending value is used up.
judgement.why: A failed body handed nothing to operations, so the submission never passes the session and CSRF checks that define when it carries and consumes the confirmation value.

topics.topic: Whether to close or drain and reuse a connection after refusing an oversized upload
questions: After an upload is refused while file bytes remain unread—because its declared length is over the limit or the received bytes exceed the limit—must Registry close the connection or drain and discard the remaining framed body before reusing it?

judgement.why: P11 asks the same unchanged question about disposing of an unread upload body after an early refusal and already records State 5's close-without-draining decision.

precedent.topic: Responsibility and method for disposing of unread upload bodies after early refusal
quotes:
After an upload's answer, whatever it was — accepted, or refused before any
or after some bytes were read — `owner_interface` discards the unread
remainder of the body without reading it into anything and closes the
connection its listener accepted; a connection that carried an upload is
never reused. A proxy or TLS terminator in front of Registry is the host's
(Explicit exclusions).
precedent.why: State 5 assigns disposal to `owner_interface`: it does not drain the unread body, closes the accepted connection, and never reuses an upload connection.

topics.topic: Which body failures are covered by the phrase “reading fails”
questions: Does “reading ... fails” mean only an I/O or HTTP-stream failure, or also failure to decode or parse a complete body into a form, service request, or upload head?

quotes:
inputs that are not of the wire
format — a body that cannot be read as it, a field it does not declare, a
value of another shape than its field's — are answered stage (1) first and
then `invalid_request` (`outside_closed_list`) at stage (4).

The CSRF value the first part carries, the delimiter that ends the file
part, and the file part's declared length — the request's declared length
less the head it read and the closing delimiter with its final `--` and line
end, or none when the request declared none; or that the head is not of that form — no multipart content type or
boundary, a first part that is not the CSRF field, no second part that is
the file — or is longer than the imported `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES`
constant, or declares less than that head and the closing delimiter, or the
request's stream fails or ends while the head is read — with none of these
values.

None: a head of another form answers no CSRF value, and the upload is
refused at stage (1) as a change without one (A04 rule 6, A13 rule 5).
judgement.why: State 5 distinguishes decoding or parsing a complete but malformed request, which produces a refusal, from a stream failure while reading the body or upload head.
